finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role; requireRole() return value is discarded, so any authenticated user can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled User u and tenant path parameter on POST /tenants/{t}/wipe (Admin.java:24-25). Precondition: caller holds any valid User, including one with no OWNER role.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at Admin.java:27 (destructive, irreversible tenant deletion).

trace.note: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe handler calls wipe(User u, String tenant) with caller-supplied values.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is evaluated, but its boolean result is not checked.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws (documented at line 13 as 'Does not throw').

finding.guards_checked: requireRole at line 26 is a non-enforcing predicate whose result is ignored. No other check exists in wipe(). No tenant-membership check. Null-user and null-roles inputs fail closed only by NPE, which is not a real guard. Compare export() at line 32, which correctly uses checkRole (throws on missing role).

verdict.guard_found: none. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and never throws, and its result is discarded at src/Admin.java:26, so wipe() runs repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 unconditionally. The only other file in the directory is src/Admin.java itself, so no route-layer role check is present in the code available. checkRole (lines 18-22) is the enforcing variant, and export() at line 32 correctly uses it.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-enforcing requireRole and discards its boolean result, so any caller with a valid User reaches the destructive repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27, while export() at line 32 uses checkRole, which throws.

finding.claim: Neither wipe() nor export() binds the caller to the target tenant, so an OWNER of one tenant can export or wipe any other tenant. Plausible only if roles are global rather than per-tenant; the role model is not visible in this code, so this is unconfirmed.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled tenant parameter (Admin.java:25 and :31) combined with a User whose roles set contains OWNER (from the caller's own account).
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at Admin.java:33 (bulk tenant data exfiltration); repo.wipe(tenant) at Admin.java:27.

trace.note: export(User u, String tenant) accepts any tenant id from the caller.
checkRole(u, "OWNER") only verifies that the global role set contains OWNER; the tenant argument is not consulted.
repo.export(tenant) runs for the arbitrary tenant id.
User carries only name and roles, with no tenant scope, so the code cannot distinguish 'OWNER of tenant A' from 'OWNER of tenant B'.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole enforces the role but not tenant ownership. No tenant-to-user membership lookup exists in this file. Whether the repo or the caller's session enforces tenant scope is not visible here; confirm against the role-assignment model and the route/filter layer.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at Admin.java:18-22 (used at :32) throws SecurityException when the role is missing, so the OWNER check on export is effective. No tenant-membership check exists in Admin.java, and no route or filter layer is in the repo. requireRole at :14-16 returns a bool that wipe() discards at :26, so it is not a guard.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate: export() at Admin.java:31-33 passes the caller-supplied tenant to repo.export after checkRole at :32 confirms only a global OWNER role, and User at :4 has no tenant scope. Whether this is cross-tenant escalation depends on whether roles are per-tenant or enforced by a route/filter layer, and neither is in the repo, so it cannot be decided here. Separately, wipe() at Admin.java:26-27 discards requireRole's boolean, so any authenticated caller with no role can wipe any tenant; that is a distinct, stronger defect the candidate does not claim.
